findings.title: The bash guard never checks where tar writes its archive, so `tar -cf <checkout>/hooks/a.py ...` creates or overwrites any file inside the protected checkout - including the maintainer's accepted.json, which the same guard refuses to `cp`
evidence: FIXED in 0.79.0. hooks/enforce_bash_scope.py:618-624 now binds `archive` from the `-f`/`--file` value, resolved against the SHELL's cwd rather than `here`, with `-f -` read as stdout; :640-649 yields it as `tar -f (writes the archive)` for every mode that is not extract, list or compare.

RE-INJECTION, not absence. Isolated scratch copy of HEAD (git archive HEAD into /private/tmp/.../scratchpad/base, PYTHONPATH=<scratch>/src ahead of the editable install, PYTHONDONTWRITEBYTECODE=1, __pycache__ swept). `import verdict_mcp` printed <scratch>/src/verdict_mcp/__init__.py, so the copy ran its own code. GREEN CONTROL FIRST: `pytest tests/test_hooks.py -k tar` -> 76 passed, 164 deselected in 3.07s.

ARM: the yield disabled (`if False and archive and not _mode(...)`) -> 6 failed, 70 passed. The failures are the six write shapes: `-cf {repo}/hooks/a.py -C {scratch} junk`, `-cf{repo}/hooks/a.py ...`, `--file={repo}/hooks/a.py -c ...`, `-c -f {repo}/hooks/a.py ...`, `-C {scratch}/junk -cf ../repo/hooks/loot.tar c.py`, `-cf {repo}/hooks/loot.tar {scratch}/junk`.

INSTRUMENT CONTROL: after the F-71 arm was run and reverted, this same injection was applied again and failed identically (6 failed, 70 passed) - so the arms are not all reading the same way and no stale bytecode is in play.

The acceptance evidence run 13 asked for is present and is by EFFECT, not by spelling: TAR_WRITE_SHAPES (tests/test_hooks.py:958-980) carries 15 rows, each asserted twice - once against the guard (test_the_guard_agrees_with_where_tar_writes) and once by running real GNU tar and diffing the checkout (test_real_tar_writes_where_this_matrix_claims). Five rows are ALLOWs that must survive, including `-C {repo}/src -cf ../scratch/y.tar b.py`, the row that distinguishes 'resolve against -C' from 'resolve against the cwd'. `_gnu_tar()` resolved to /opt/homebrew/bin/gtar (GNU tar 1.35) here, so the real-tar half ran rather than skipping.
Also pinned: eval/pinned_mutants.json entries `0.79.0 S2` and `0.79.0 S3`, both re-run independently this run against the whole 888-test suite and both KILLED (7 failed and 2 failed respectively).

The `--directory` full spelling row still passes in the arm, which is the differential that identifies the mechanism: the rule reached the two spellings nobody uses and none of the abbreviations everybody does.

findings.title: The bash guard reads a git flag or sub-verb name ANYWHERE in the argument list, whatever role it plays there, so one ordinary token disarms the check for every mutating verb: `git commit -m "--dry-run"` really commits and `git branch -D <branch> list` really deletes, both with the guard's blessing
evidence: SITE 1 - hooks/enforce_bash_scope.py:487 `if any(t in ("--dry-run", "--check") for t in args): return`. The scan runs before the verb is even identified and matches a token in ANY role, including an option's VALUE. `git commit -m "--dry-run"` therefore returns early and yields no target at all.

SITE 2 - hooks/enforce_bash_scope.py:511 `if any(t in _GIT_READONLY_SUBVERBS.get(verb, set()) for t in rest): return`. For `branch` and `tag` the read-only name is `list`, but for those verbs a bare positional is the NAME TO CREATE, so the token that proves read-only intent for `stash` is an operand for `branch`.

PROVEN, guard half, with a control. Asked of the live hook (VERDICT_STRICT=1, cwd = this checkout) by piping the PreToolUse event to hooks/enforce_bash_scope.py: DENY `git commit -am wip`, DENY `git stash`, DENY `git stash push -m wip`, DENY `git checkout -- .`, DENY `git reset --hard HEAD list` - the instrument is not waving everything through. Then: ALLOW `git commit -am "--dry-run"`, ALLOW `git commit -m --dry-run`, ALLOW `git stash push -m "--dry-run"`, ALLOW `git tag -a v9 -m --dry-run`, ALLOW `git push origin main --check`, ALLOW `git branch list`, ALLOW `git branch -D main list`, ALLOW `git branch -M evil list`, ALLOW `git tag list`, ALLOW `git tag -d v0.79.0 list`, ALLOW `git worktree remove /tmp/x list`, ALLOW `git notes add -m x list`.

PROVEN, effect half, in a throwaway git repository under the scratch directory - never this checkout. (a) `git -C <victim> branch -D keepme list` -> the guard allowed it, git printed "error: branch 'list' not found" AND "Deleted branch keepme (was ebcdfcd)"; `for-each-ref refs/heads` went from {keepme, main} to {main}. The trailing token errors after the deletion has already happened. (b) CONTROL: `git -C <victim> commit --allow-empty -m wip` -> DENIED by the guard, reason "git commit (mutates the checkout) targets '<victim>' (a git checkout under /private/tmp)". (c) ARM: the identical command with the message changed to the literal `--dry-run` -> the guard allowed it and git answered `[main a2f5313] --dry-run`, rc=0. One word of a commit message is the whole difference between deny and commit.

MECHANISM: `_check_git` decides read-only-ness by SET MEMBERSHIP over a flat token list. Membership is a property of the string; being a flag, a sub-verb or a value is a property of its POSITION. The function never reads position, so any command may claim either property by carrying the word.

CLASS - searched, and the permitting direction is exactly these two lines: `grep -n 'for t in args|for t in rest|in args\b|in rest\b' hooks/enforce_bash_scope.py` returns 11 hits; nine are in the OVER-yielding direction (`"-delete" in args`, `"--remove-source-files" in args`, the sed/perl and awk scans), which can only add a candidate target. Only :487 and :511 return early, and both are in `_check_git`. Same mechanism, same fix, one finding.

LATENT CONDITION: tests/test_hooks.py's git coverage asserts spellings that SHOULD be denied and spellings that SHOULD be allowed, but never a denied command with an allowed token appended. The 888-test suite is green with this hole open, and `git commit` is the first entry on this project's own forbidden-commands list (.qa/profile.md).

SEVERITY, held honestly. Critical because the guard IS this product's authorization control - the profile names it risk area 1, 'a bypass silently removes the product's core safety guarantee' - and this is a proven bypass reaching `git commit`, `git stash push` (which destroys uncommitted work) and `git branch -D`. P1 rather than P0 because nothing is presently breaking: the guard is documented defence-in-depth whose model already excludes interpreter escapes (`sh script.sh`, `python -c`), so this lowers the bar for a determined agent rather than granting a capability it lacked, and an accidental trigger needs a literal `--dry-run` token in a value. Run 13 filed comparable tar bypasses as Major; I depart because those needed an unusual command shape aimed at one effect, while this disarms EVERY mutating git verb through an ordinary token. What would make it P0: evidence that a realistic agent command shape hits it without intent, or a decision to state the guard as an adversarial control.

root_cause.mechanism: `_check_git` establishes 'this command only reads' by testing set membership over a flat token list (:487 for `--dry-run`/`--check`, :511 for the per-verb read-only sub-verbs). Membership is a property of the string; flag-vs-sub-verb-vs-value is a property of position, which the function never reads. Both tests `return` early, so a matching token suppresses the yield that would have produced a target.
root_cause.origin: Both lines predate this range. :509-510's own comment records why the sub-verb set exists - `git config --get user.name` was being denied - so the set was widened to fix a false positive and the widening was written as an unpositioned membership test.

class.pattern: role-blind token membership decides a whole command's classification

root_cause.trigger: Nothing in this range. Found by a QA session probing the guard's git handling after `git branch --show-current` was refused (VERDICT-F-76, the same mechanism seen from the other side).
root_cause.latent_condition: No test in the suite appends an allowed token to a denied command. Every git assertion is a whole spelling that is either denied or allowed, so the axis 'what else is on the line' has no row - the same blind spot run 13's lesson identified in the tar matrix, one function above it.

proof.evidence: Identical `git -C <victim> commit --allow-empty` denied with message `wip` and allowed - and executed, `[main a2f5313] --dry-run` - with message `--dry-run`; `git -C <victim> branch -D keepme list` allowed and `keepme` gone from refs/heads.

findings.outcome_reason: still open; nothing has settled it

findings.title: The same role-blind membership test denies read-only git commands the sub-verb set was written to allow: `git branch --show-current`, `git branch -v`, `git tag --list` and `git config --get-regexp` are all refused as checkout mutations
evidence: hooks/enforce_bash_scope.py:511 matches the LITERAL strings in `_GIT_READONLY_SUBVERBS`. For `branch`, `tag`, `worktree`, `notes` and `sparse-checkout` the set holds bare words (`list`, `status`, `show`), so the dashed spellings git actually uses miss. `config` is the only verb whose set carries both forms (`get`, `list`, `--get`, `--list`, `--get-all`, `-l`) - and it is the one the comment at :509 says the set was written for.

MEASURED against the live hook, with a control: DENY `git branch --show-current`, DENY `git branch -v`, DENY `git branch --list`, DENY `git tag --list`, DENY `git config --get-regexp user`; ALLOW `git worktree list --porcelain`, ALLOW `git submodule status`, ALLOW `git config --get user.name` - the three whose read-only word happens to be bare.

COST MEASURED THIS SESSION, not hypothesised: `git branch --show-current` was refused during this run and had to be worked around with `git rev-parse --abbrev-ref HEAD`. The guard's own comment at :509-510 states the stake: 'Denying `git config --get user.name` would be the kind of false positive that gets strict mode switched off.'

Minor rather than Major because a read-only workaround exists for every case (`rev-parse`, `for-each-ref`, `config --get`), so the cost is friction rather than lost capability. What would raise it: a report that strict mode was disabled because of it.
findings.outcome_reason: still open; nothing has settled it

findings.title: Every non-dash argument of a generic mutator is treated as a path, so a mode or owner operand is resolved against the cwd: `chmod +x <scratch>/x.sh` is denied because `+x` resolves to `<checkout>/+x` - and so is `chmod +x .qa/x.sh`, inside the QA root the agent may write
evidence: hooks/enforce_bash_scope.py:727-730 - the `_MUTATORS` fallback is `for t in args: if not t.startswith("-"): yield head, t`. `chmod`, `chown`, `truncate` and `install` all take a non-path first operand (mode, owner, size), and none of those start with `-`.

MEASURED against the live hook, with a control: DENY `chmod +x /private/tmp/claude-501/x.sh`, DENY `chmod 755 /private/tmp/claude-501/x.sh`, DENY `chown artjack /private/tmp/claude-501/x.sh`, DENY `truncate -s 0 /private/tmp/claude-501/x.txt`, DENY `chmod +x .qa/x.sh`; ALLOW `rm /private/tmp/claude-501/x.sh` - the same temp path, so the denial is the mode operand and not the file.

COST MEASURED THIS SESSION: `chmod +x <scratch>/run_arm.sh` was refused, with the reason "chmod targets '<checkout>/+x'", and the whole compound Bash call - including the heredoc that had already been written into it - was blocked before anything ran.
`.qa/x.sh` being denied is the sharper half: the guard refuses to chmod a file inside the one directory it exists to permit.
P3 because `bash script.sh` avoids it entirely and no safety property is weakened - this is the over-yielding, conservative direction of the same role-blindness as VERDICT-F-75.
findings.outcome_reason: still open; nothing has settled it

findings.title: Two of the four release-workflow tests read the job text including COMMENTS, so the sha256 check that VERDICT-F-73's fix rests on can be deleted and replaced by a comment that merely names it, and all four tests stay green
evidence: tests/test_release_workflow.py:22-25 defines `_commands(job)` - 'The lines that run - comments explaining what NOT to do are not evidence' - and only two of the four tests use it. `test_the_download_is_checksummed_before_it_runs` (:33-41) and `test_a_registry_failure_is_visible` (:44-49) both call `_registry_job()` raw.

PROVEN by injection in an isolated scratch copy of HEAD, after a green control (4 passed). The line `echo "${MCP_PUBLISHER_SHA256}  mcp-publisher.tar.gz" | sha256sum -c -` was replaced by the comment `# sha256sum -c - runs in CI hardening, see below`. Result: 4 passed in 0.01s. The workflow no longer verifies anything and the suite says the supply chain is pinned.

DIFFERENTIAL that names the mechanism: the catalogue's own mutant `0.79.0 S9` deletes the same line OUTRIGHT (new: "") and is KILLED. The kill therefore measures 'the string is absent', not 'the check runs' - which is the distinction `_commands` was written to make.
The same weakness applies to `test_a_registry_failure_is_visible`, which accepts `::error::` and `exit 1` found in a comment.

CLASS - this is the third time this shape has been filed in this repository: VERDICT-F-64 (the 3.9 floor test asked whether a string appeared anywhere in the file) and VERDICT-F-60's utf8_stderr pair (an AST check that watches the call, not the behaviour). A test that greps a file for the name of the thing it wants is this project's most repeated assertion defect.
FIX: change both tests to read `_commands(_registry_job())`, and add the comment-only variant above as a regression row - the injection is already written. Two words plus one test.
Major by the fix-today bar: it is a two-word change, and until it lands the supply-chain control the release just shipped has no guard against silent removal.
findings.outcome_reason: still open; nothing has settled it

findings.title: The import census matches `from`/`import` as text over added lines, so prose in a module docstring is reported as an undeclared dependency - this range's only census lead is a sentence
evidence: src/verdict_mcp/census.py:47 `_PY_IMPORT = re.compile(r"^\s*(?:from|import)\s+([A-Za-z_][A-Za-z0-9_]*)")`, applied line by line to the added lines of a diff with no notion of strings or comments.

MEASURED in this run's own .qa/facts.json: `code_census.imports.undeclared = {"a": ["tests/test_release_workflow.py:4"]}`. Line 4 of that file is inside the module docstring and reads 'from a `releases/latest` URL, with no checksum, in a job holding an OIDC'. The census reported the English word 'a' as an undeclared import root.
That is the ONLY import lead this range produced, so the channel's signal this run is 0 of 1.

The module discloses the risk ('candidates, not convictions'), which is why this is Minor and not Major - but a lead channel whose leads are prose is a channel a reader learns to skip, and §4.5 of the agent contract tells the agent to spend reading budget on it.

FIX: require the rest of the line to look like an import - `^\s*(?:from\s+([\w.]+)\s+import\b|import\s+([\w.]+))` - or parse the added file with `ast` and read `Import`/`ImportFrom` nodes, which also removes comments and strings for free.
findings.outcome_reason: still open; nothing has settled it

findings.title: Fix verification picks its test by scraping any pytest node id out of a finding's prose evidence, so a mis-scraped id that fails at HEAD force-reopens a correctly-resolved finding over the tester's judgment
evidence: THE FLATTERING HALF IS CLOSED by 0.79.0 (VERDICT-F-72): a `first_cited` pick can no longer write `fix_verified`, a 'verification (measured)' evidence line, or a confirmed/measured row in the ledger. Verified by re-injection this run.

THE REMAINING HALF IS NOW A STATED DESIGN POSITION, not an oversight. src/verdict_mcp/harness.py:537 still reads `if how == 'first_cited' and len(tests) > 1:`, so ONE prose id is still run and may still refuse a resolution; harness.py:651-657 says so in a comment and CHANGELOG 0.79.0 says so in prose ('A single prose-cited test may still refuse - a finding held open costs a re-read').

IT MIS-SELECTED AGAIN THIS RUN, the sixth consecutive run. This run's own .qa/facts.json: `verification.VERDICT-F-26 = {test: 'tests/test_validate.py::test_the_state_validator_keeps_checking_after_a_malformed_entry', selected_by: 'first_cited', candidates: 1, at_previous: 'pass', at_head: 'pass'}`. That test is about the state validator continuing past a malformed entry and has nothing to do with the selector; it is in this finding's evidence only because run 12 quoted it AS the example of a mis-scrape.

WHAT IS ACTUALLY LEFT, stated precisely, because the severity turns on it: (a) a record naming an unrelated test is attached to this finding in state.json every run - now disclosed, since `verification_notes` this run reads '1 finding(s) verified on a test cited only in prose (VERDICT-F-26)'; (b) a single unrelated test that FAILS at HEAD can still force a correctly-resolved finding back to open with a `resolution_refused` sentence that is false about that finding. (b) has never actually happened in 14 runs.

SEVERITY LOWERED Major -> Minor this run, deliberately and with the id and first_seen unchanged. The half that corrupted the track record is gone; the half that remains errs toward holding findings open, which is the safe direction, and the maintainer has documented it as the intended trade. What would raise it back to Major: one real run in which an unrelated cited test force-reopens a finding that was genuinely fixed.

TWO WAYS TO CLOSE IT, and the second is not a code change: (1) apply `unselectable` at any candidate count - change `len(tests) > 1` to `len(tests) >= 1` at harness.py:537, which is the whole fix; or (2) if the maintainer stands by the design, record it with `verdict-accept` so it stops carrying as an open finding for a seventh run. This project built an accepted-risk mechanism in 0.78.0 for exactly this situation.
findings.outcome_reason: still open; nothing has settled it

findings.title: The instrument control §3 prescribes for the stale-bytecode fault cannot fire in the ordering that produced VERDICT-F-50: re-running an injection you already watched fail reads FAIL while the shadowed bytecode is still what runs
evidence: Untouched by this range, and confirmed rather than assumed: `git diff --stat 0892869..4dc006a -- agents/ standards/ templates/ commands/` returns nothing. CHANGELOG 0.79.0 states it explicitly: 'the prompt is byte-identical' and 'F-58 and the one-sentence `accepted` teaching remain the queued, eval-paid prompt release'.
The queue behind the single eval payment is unchanged at two items: F-58's instrument-control clause, and 0.78.0's admission that the model meets `status: accepted` and delta `ACCEPTED` untaught.

This run supplies a datum the prompt release should use. The contract's control ('re-run an injection you have already watched fail, and if it now passes, you are measuring the cache') was exercised for real here: F-70's injection was re-applied after the F-71 arm and failed identically (6 failed, 70 passed). It worked because the arms are subprocess-executed hook scripts under PYTHONDONTWRITEBYTECODE=1 with __pycache__ swept between arms - i.e. the control passed because the fault was already excluded by other means, which is exactly the blind spot this finding names.
Not re-reproduced this run. Run 12 reproduced it at HEAD in F-50's exact ordering and nothing in the range touches the mechanism. Held as unchanged, not as re-measured.
findings.outcome_reason: still open; nothing has settled it

findings.title: Eleven rules shipped in 0.74.0 survive mutation against the whole suite, including the only call site of the `__pycache__` sweep, the whole UTF-8 stderr fix, both `_ago` boundaries and `run_date`'s offset normalisation
evidence: RE-MEASURED AT RUN-14 HEAD, against 888 tests rather than 850. Isolated scratch copy of HEAD, PYTHONPATH ahead of the editable install, PYTHONDONTWRITEBYTECODE=1, __pycache__ swept, 1.1s between same-size edits, green control first: 888 passed in 89.51s. All five sampled survivors SURVIVE again: (6) utf8_stderr body -> pass: 888 passed in 88.16s. (7) errors='replace' -> 'strict': 888 passed in 90.22s. (8) _ago `minutes < 60` -> `<= 60`: 888 passed in 89.72s. (9) _ago `age_h >= 1.05` -> `> 1.05`: 888 passed in 89.01s. (10) run_date `stamp.replace('Z','+00:00')` -> `stamp.replace('Z','')`: 888 passed in 88.92s. The range added 38 tests and not one of them touches these lines.

CORRECTION TO RUN 13, and it changes the work this finding asks for. Run 13 put survivor (10) at the top of the next-run focus, reasoning that 'dropping the offset makes a timestamped-with-offset run fall back to datetime.now(timezone.utc).date() silently'. That is wrong. (10) IS AN EQUIVALENT MUTANT. Driven directly over nine stamps, the two versions return the same date for every well-formed input: '2026-09-05T23:30:00Z' -> 2026-09-05 both ways; '2026-09-05T23:30:00-07:00' -> 2026-09-06 both ways (the mutant does not touch a `-07:00` string at all); '' and 'garbage' -> the now() fallback both ways. They differ on exactly one input, the malformed '2026-09-05T23:30:00Z+01:00'. `datetime.fromisoformat` parses a naive stamp happily, so the ValueError branch run 13's reasoning depends on is never reached. No test can be written for a difference that does not exist.

THE HONEST READING OF THE FIVE, which is what the next run should act on: 1 is equivalent - (10); 2 are Windows-only behaviour this macOS suite structurally cannot observe - (6) and (7), the utf8_stderr pair, whose AST check watches the CALL and not the BEHAVIOUR; and 2 are genuine unpinned boundaries - (8) at exactly 60 minutes ('60 minutes ago' vs '1 hour ago') and (9) at exactly age_h == 1.05 ('1.1 hours ago' vs '1 hour ago'). Two of eleven are cheap, real and testable today; one is not testable at all; one is not a defect.

next_run_focus: VERDICT-F-75 first, and it is one function. `_check_git` decides read-only-ness by asking whether a WORD is present; it must ask what ROLE the word plays. Concretely: (a) drop the blanket `--dry-run`/`--check` prescan at :487 and let each verb declare which of its own flags are non-mutating, checked after the verb is known and never against a token that follows an option that takes a value (`-m`, `-F`, `--message`, `-o`); (b) at :511, match the read-only sub-verb only at the FIRST positional after the verb, and hold both spellings (`list` and `--list`) as `config` already does. The acceptance evidence is not another list of spellings - run 13's lesson applies here verbatim: enumerate by EFFECT and add the axis no row has, which is 'a denied command with an allowed token appended'. One row per verb: `git commit -m "--dry-run"`, `git stash push -m "--dry-run"`, `git branch -D x list`, `git tag -d v9 list`, `git worktree remove /tmp/x list`, `git notes add -m x list`, each asserted DENY, and the read-only forms of VERDICT-F-76 each asserted ALLOW in the same table.

caveats: `confirmed` means fix-verified or regressed; it therefore tracks which findings held up under a check, not correctness in the abstract
still-open findings are undecided on purpose and are excluded from every rate rather than guessed at
a resolution nobody checked at all stays undecided: absence is not proof

`confirmed` is split by `outcome_basis`: `measured` is the harness's own re-injection, `claimed` is the tester's, weighed only by the absence of a measurement that contradicts it — read the two numbers separately
`accepted` is a third basis: the maintainer confirmed the defect and declined the fix (`verdict-accept`) — the finding held up on their word, not under a check
